chunks: Tawhid al-Saduq: From al-Attar, from Sa'd, from Ibn Yazid, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Nine things have been raised (excused) from my Umma: error, forgetfulness, what they were coerced to do, what they do not have the strength for, what they are ignorant of, what they have to do out of necessity, jealousy, bad omen, and thinking about the whispered prompts in regards the creation – so long as it is not voiced by the tongue.
ai.seo_question: What are the nine things for which Muslims are excused according to this hadith from Tawhid al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Shaykh al-Saduq, outlines the nine categories of exemption (afwat) from divine accountability, emphasizing that spiritual liability requires both capacity and conscious intent. It distinguishes between involuntary states like error and forgetfulness, and internal dispositions like jealousy and superstition, noting that the latter only incur guilt if verbalized, a nuance significant in Shia jurisprudence for determining the scope of sin. The narration underscores the divine mercy inherent in the legal theory of 'removal of burden' (raf' al-haraj), ensuring that believers are not punished for what lies beyond their control.
